thread:
incident-bot: Pager alert: elevated error rate 502 from eu-west1 -> Possible regional routing failure
Alice Perez: seeing 30% 5xx across eu-west1 model endpoints, load balancer health checks flipping. Kicking off incident.
SRE-oncall: I'm on it. Can someone confirm whether this is LB health-check or instance-level? ...
Netops Jay: Confirming from VPC flow logs: heavy ECMP imbalance; a subset of routes to eu-west1 are blackholing returning traffic after transient MTU change. Cloud provider acknowledged 'fabric reroute' on 3 AZs in eu-west1. This explains asymmetric TCP flows causing health checks to fail.
Alice Perez: Impact: customer requests routed to eu-west1 are getting 502s and long tails. Some customers reporting elevated latency and partial failures. Product Sam, can you get a quick customer impact note? 
Product Sam: Noted. Drafting: "We are investigating a regional routing issue affecting requests from EU; retries may be going to other regions. Engineers are actively mitigating." Will ping customers on P0 apps.
Support Maya: Getting multiple tickets from EU accounts. Marking all P1. Prioritizing enterprise customers behind dedicated capacity.
SRE-oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) Stop new traffic to eu-west1 via traffic-shift; 2) Drain existing connections; 3) Route customers to us-central1/uk-south fallback pools; 4) Run health-check fix once fabric is stable.
eng-runtime: For draining, note that long-lived streaming connections persist. We need a graceful termination policy in gateway. Starting connection-drainer job.
Netops Jay: Executing traffic shift now: 
```
rwctl traffic shift --from eu-west1 --to us-central1 --percent 100 --mode immediate --reason "fabric route flap"
``` 
SRE-oncall: Shift command accepted. Observing slow propagation in DNS caches due to 300s TTL on internal proxy SRV records — some edge proxies still prefer eu-west1.
dns-bot: DNS change queued: lowering TTL to 30s for affected proxies. Propagation may take up to existing TTL window. 
Alice Perez: Workaround: adding explicit route policy to edge gateway to prefer us-central1 for the next 15 minutes. Applying now.
eng-runtime: Noted. Starting forced connection migration for streaming sessions older than 5m to avoid stuck connections.
SRE-oncall: FYI some backends in eu-west1 marked unhealthy due to health-check source IP hash mismatch after provider-side SNAT change. That caused cascading LB failover attempts which spiked control plane calls.
Netops Jay: Provider confirms SNAT/egress IP behavior changed during reroute — they're rolling back. Meanwhile I'm increasing LB health-check timeout to 10s to reduce flapping.
Alice Perez: Can we confirm customer impact windows and which tenants hit dedicated capacity? Support Maya please compile list and escalate.
Support Maya: Sent list of 7 enterprise tenants; three had failures >5min. I'm opening dedicated-support-bridge with account owners. 
Product Sam: Notifying impacted customers with status page update. ETA for full recovery depends on route stabilization; estimate 15-45 minutes.
SRE-oncall: Monitoring metrics: errors in EU down from 30% to 8% after partial shift. Still seeing 502 spikes from edge proxies with cached routes.
Netops Jay: Cache purge pushed to CDN/edge for affected prefixes. Also removed ephemeral BGP route that was causing suboptimal path.
Alice Perez: Heads-up: the drain job found ~200 stuck streaming sessions; moving them to fallback required token refresh for some clients. eng-runtime handling token refresh on-the-fly.
eng-runtime: Implemented token refresh in migration path. Running small canary for 10 connections.
SRE-oncall: Canary looks good. Increasing cutover. 
incident-bot: Incident transitioned to mitigation state by SRE-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/regional-failover
Alice Perez: Handing incident to night-shift oncall in 30m. @sre-night please prepare to monitor and escalate if provider rollback incomplete.
SRE-oncall: Handoff: created follow-up tasks and timeline in the incident doc. All key contacts tagged.
sre-night: Ack, taking oncall in 30m. Will continue monitoring for residual failovers and confirm DNS TTL fully propagated.
Product Sam: Postmortem note: primary cause appears to be provider fabric reroute + SNAT behavior change which created asymmetric flows and LB health-check failures leading to unhealthy failovers. Action items: 1) Add cross-region connection sanity checks; 2) Reduce internal DNS TTLs for failover-critical records; 3) Improve streaming connection migration path.
Alice Perez: Thanks everyone. Support, please finish outbound comms. Netops, keep provider engaged until rollback complete.
Support Maya: Outbound updates sent. Customers acknowledged and appreciate the quick mitigation. Closing bridge once eu-west1 stable for 30m.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: eu-west1 routes stable, traffic returned under controlled rollout at 1745013200. Closing in 1h if no regression.
